metadata.evidence: We evaluate our pre-trained sparse autoencoders on the downstream tasks of denoising (for MNIST and our custom ImageNet patches dataset) and classification in the low-data regime (for MNIST only).
Alternatively, ```eval_denoising.py``` can be used given a pre-trained autoencoder.
Step 1: Given a pre-trained encoder, ```compute_codes.py``` can be used to create a dataset containing the codes for each MNIST image.
metadata.reason: Script for computing codes for classification evaluation.

metadata.evidence: Step 2: Using the dataset from the previous step, ```eval_classification.py``` can be used to measure classification performance with a set number of training samples per class.
a classifier which uses a randomly initialized LISTA encoder module followed by a linear classification layer (located in ```modles/lista_classifier.py```)
